# FieldShore v4 — Pre-Phase-J Deep Review — 2026-07-04

**Target:** `v4-redesign` @ `b8b43e1` (468 commits since the v3.19.1 fork; 46 commits since the 2026-07-01 audit).
**Question:** is the v4 code sound enough to enter Phase J (cutover, #138)?
**Method:** 14 shard×lens finder agents over `src/` (443 files / ~57k lines) + shipping config, each
scoped so no reviewer held the whole branch; plain-code dedup; a referee pass against the
known-findings baseline (June-14 build audit, #408, #410, #399/#400 sim findings, 26 open issues);
then adversarial verification — Critical/High findings judged by 3 independent lenses
(correctness / reproduce-from-code / severity-honesty, strict majority), Medium/Low by a skeptic
prompted to refute. **No fixes applied.**

**Funnel:** 81 raw findings → 70 after code dedup → 57 verified (2 auto-classified known-open,
11 referee-deduped) → **53 confirmed, 4 refuted, 0 left unverified**. All 88 agents completed.

Known gap: the 2026-07-01 autonomous audit's REPORT.md exists only on Alex's machine (untracked),
so dedup ran against its GitHub-issue record (#408/#410) + the June-14 report, not the file itself.

## Bottom line (go / no-go)

**Mechanical health: GO.** Typecheck clean, 1184/1185 tests green, the safety-math engine core
is verified **clean and complete** (the #410-1 unfloored-capacity fix is done across `capacity`,
`capacityAll`, and the LongShore unrated-zone gate), and all three June-14 build-audit **Criticals
are confirmed fixed** (Slider `pointercancel` is now snap-back-only; the soft-deleted-group gate and
inline-deploy swallow are gone). The foundation is solid and the trajectory is good.

**Cutover readiness: NO-GO yet — a focused fix-list, not a structural problem.** 8 High findings
gate Phase J, in three clusters:

1. **Safety-verdict "false-SAFE / hidden-flag" class is not fully closed** (the exact class #408/#410
   chased). Three High findings: per-strut load share divides by *planned* not *deployed* strut count
   (a partially-deployed group reads "within capacity" while one strut carries the whole load); the
   persistent over-capacity/unrated flag renders **only on the Board card**, so the same shore reads
   clean in the new List and Division views; and the #410-3 grouped-edit fan-out is **incomplete for
   mixed-status groups** (a re-measure silently diverges deployed legs from pending ones).
2. **Department/RBAC/sync governance breaks against production RTDB.** `roles/$roleId` has no
   `.write` rule → the entire ADR-017 custom-role feature is dead (every create/edit is
   PERMISSION_DENIED; delete half-applies). Dept create/join have no retry → a dept created or joined
   through one connectivity hiccup is permanently local-only with a dead invite code and a forever-
   retrying banner, and a revoked/re-joining member is wedged in an infinite "you're offline" loop.
3. **One data-integrity strand:** `commitMany` bypasses the delete-stock guard that `doCommit` got in
   the July fix, so a grouped delete on a mixed-status shore strands deployed inventory — the exact
   thing that guard was added to prevent.

Below High: **28 Medium + 17 Low**, concentrated in security-rule gaps (irrevocable invite codes,
manageUsers→Admin self-promotion, v3's permissive legacy rules deployed into the v4 project, CSV
formula-injection), offline/sync robustness (silent hangs, swallowed failures), and catalog-mode
verdict consistency. None is individually a cutover blocker, but the security-rule subset should be
fixed before real multi-department use.

**Recommendation:** treat this as the pre-cutover punch-list. Convert the 8 High + the security-rule
Mediums into tracked sub-issues under the Phase J audit gates (#256 parity, #257 XSS/security, #258
WCAG, #260 SME), fix them, re-verify the safety cluster, then re-open the go/no-go. The remaining
Mediums/Lows can ride the normal backlog.

## Confirmed High findings (8) — cutover gate

### H1 · Per-strut load share divides by *planned* group size, not *deployed* struts → false "within capacity"
`src/ui/operations/shoreSafety.ts:43` · category: safety-math · verified 3/3
- **Evidence:** `shoreSafety.ts:43` uses `strutLoadShare(sp)` where `core/shorepoint/reducer.ts:107` is `(sp.estimatedLoad ?? 0) / (sp.groupTotal ?? 1)`. `groupTotal` is the **planned** member count stamped at creation (`AssignEquipmentSheet.tsx:200 groupTotal: targetTotal`), never the count actually deployed. The store deploy gate uses the same math (`reducer.ts:93`). Partial deploys are a designed path (`AssignEquipmentSheet.tsx:249 else break; // stock exhausted`), and a lone deployed member can advance alone (`operation/reducer.ts:85`).
- **Failure:** T-Shore, load 34,000 lb, LS 406 rated 22,000. Operator taps "Add 1 more strut — deploy as Double-T" with only 1 in stock. `groupTotal=2`; member 1 deploys (share 17,000 ≤ 22,000, no ack), member 2 aborts and stays Pending. The single standing strut — physically alone under 34,000 lb — reads "Within rated capacity — 22,000 lb per strut" in Quick View, shows no board over-capacity flag, and its deploy event carries no acknowledgment. Same for a 3-Post deployed 1-of-3.
- **Note:** this challenges #408's shipped equal-split-by-`groupTotal` design specifically for *partially*-deployed groups. Share should divide by the count actually standing, or a short-of-plan group should force the over-capacity ack.

### H2 · Persistent over-capacity/unrated flag renders only on the Board card — List & Division views read clean
`src/ui/operations/ShorePointListRow.tsx:27` · category: safety-math · verified 3/3
- **Evidence:** `ShorePointCard.tsx:192,294` computes and renders the flag (`deployedCapacityFlag(sp)` → `⚠ Unrated / Over capacity`), but `ShorePointListRow.tsx:27-48` and `DivisionView.tsx:62-91` render seq/location/type/model/measurement/status only — neither calls `deployedCapacityFlag` or `shoreSafety`. `shoreSafety.ts:9-11` documents the intended contract that "a point flags identically wherever it shows" — the two new tri-view surfaces do not honor it.
- **Failure:** a LongShore in the unrated zone (or an over-capacity strut) shows "⚠ Unrated"/"⚠ Over capacity" on its Board card (the July audit-#7 v3-parity fix) but nothing at all in the List view or the Division overview — two of the three coordinated reads of the same points. The tri-view redesign (#320) silently shrank a physical-check-this-shore signal to one of three views. Re-breaks the #410-7 at-a-glance guarantee.

### H3 · #410-3 grouped-edit fan-out incomplete — mixed-status groups still diverge silently
`src/ui/operations/AddShorePointModal.tsx:451` · category: status-changed · verified 3/3
- **Evidence:** `handleSaveEdit` computes `members` as ALL live group-mates and fans the same `ShorePointEdited` patch to each (line 451), and the comment (446-449) claims this prevents divergence. But `core/shorepoint/reducer.ts:233` `applyPatch` silently drops the sizing fields for any non-pending mate: `if (sp.status !== 'pending') return next;` — `measurementEighths`/`deductions`/`division` are applied only below that line. No mixed-status guard/warning; `ShorePointEdited` is a plain-append (commit reports ok).
- **Failure:** 3-Post with leg 1 already Equipment-Assigned, legs 2-3 Pending. Operator re-measures and edits leg 2 (`measurementEighths 384→372`). Legs 2-3 update to 46.5″; leg 1 silently stays 48″. One physical shore now carries two required lengths → different strut recs and different Cutting-Station cut lengths. The July audit-#3 / #410-3 fix (`79172b9`) covered only all-pending groups (its test `AddShorePointModal.test.tsx:374-394` asserts exactly that case).

### H4 · `roles/$roleId` has no `.write` rule — custom-role RBAC is dead against production RTDB
`src/core/schema/rules.ts:276` · category: security · verified 3/3
- **Evidence:** `rules.ts:276 deptNode['roles'] = { $roleId: objectRules(RoleNode) }` — `objectRules()` emits only `.validate` + `$other`, never `.write` (rules.ts:62-78). The only ancestor grant is the dept node's CREATE_ONLY `.write` (false once the dept exists). Committed `database.rules.json` confirms no `.write` under the roles subtree. Yet the shipped User Manager writes it: `departmentService.ts:514` (createRole `set`), `:537` (editRole update), `:564` (deleteRole remove), wired at `UserManagerScreen.tsx:277` / `router.tsx:134` (`/users`). `deleteRole` reassigns holders **first** (members `.write` succeeds), then the role `remove()` is denied → half-applied. `rules.test.ts` asserts only the role `.validate` shape — never a write (the "untested rule" class the file's own L-11 header forbids).
- **Failure:** a founding Admin creates a custom role → default-deny → "You don't have permission." Editing Default's permissions: same. Deleting a role: every holder is silently moved to Default (succeeds), then the remove is denied — the role survives with zero holders, no audit trail. The entire ADR-017 feature is non-functional in production.

### H5 · Department created without cloud reachability never reaches the cloud — no retry, dead invite code
`src/data/dept/departmentService.ts:207` · category: sync · verified 3/3
- **Evidence:** `departmentService.ts:206-214` — the `set(orgs/${id}, payload)` catch **logs and returns `ok:true`**; no path ever re-pushes the dept node or the invite-code resolver (the comment defers retry to "Engine A", not landed). Because `EVENT_WRITE`/`stateWrite` require `orgs/$deptId/members/$uid` to exist (rules.ts:97-99,149,174), a dept with no cloud node makes every later event/state upload PERMISSION_DENIED forever (flush keeps them queued; banner shows "retrying" indefinitely). The catch's offline assumption is also wrong for the real transport: an offline RTDB `set()` doesn't reject — it buffers pending — so a truly-offline create hangs at the await, and a reload before reconnect discards the buffered write into the same permanently-unsynced state.
- **Failure:** a founder creates a department on degraded connectivity and reloads before the write lands. The dept exists locally, the success sheet shows an invite code that resolves to nothing ("that code isn't valid"), and every operation event fails upload forever behind an eternal "N changes haven't synced — retrying" banner. Nothing self-heals.

### H6 · `joinByCode` misreads PERMISSION_DENIED as "offline" — revoked/re-joining members wedged in an infinite loop
`src/data/dept/departmentService.ts:321` · category: sync · verified 3/3
- **Evidence:** `departmentService.ts:308-327` — the member-row write's catch unconditionally `queueJoin(...)` and returns `queued:true, reason:"You're offline…"`. But `JOIN_SELF_WRITE` (rules.ts:112-119) requires `!data.exists()`, so any **existing** member row (a revoked member with `active:false`, or a legit member on a new device whose `recoverDeptFromCloud` returned null) is PERMISSION_DENIED while fully online. `retryPendingJoin` (335-350) only clears the intent when `!result.queued` — this path returns `queued:true`, so every reconnect re-resolves the (still-active) code, re-fails, re-queues forever. The `writeError()` helper (375-379) already distinguishes `permission_denied`; the join path predates it. `departmentService.test.ts:259-266` bakes the misclassification in.
- **Failure:** a member revoked via User Manager (or joining on a new device) types their code while online → denied → app says "You're offline, you'll join when you reconnect" while online; the pendingJoin banner persists forever; every reconnect retries and re-queues. The user never joins and never learns they were revoked.

### H7 · `commitMany` bypasses the ShorePointDeleted stock guard — grouped delete strands deployed inventory
`src/data/store/operationStore.ts:305` · category: data-integrity · verified 3/3
- **Evidence:** `doCommit` guards it (`operationStore.ts:262 if (sp && sp.deployedBom && sp.status !== 'returned') return {ok:false, …}`), but `doCommitMany`'s type gate (305-314) rejects only the six inventory-consequential event types — `ShorePointDeleted` is not among them — then `db.events.bulkAdd(...)` lands unguarded. `DeleteShorePointModal.tsx:31-36` builds the batch from all live group members with no status filter and uses `commitMany` when `members.length > 1`. Mixed pending/deployed groups are reachable (`AssignEquipmentSheet.tsx:238-249` partial deploy). The reducer soft-deletes regardless of status.
- **Failure:** a 3-Post deploys 2 members, 1 stays Pending. The Pending card offers Delete → confirming batch-deletes all 3. The two deployed members carry `deployedBom` with stock already decremented; they vanish into the Deleted section, their struts/plates stay decremented with no visible deployment and no return path. Inventory is wrong until someone restores and individually returns each — exactly what the July audit-#6 guard (`79172b9`) was meant to prevent; the guard was added to `doCommit` only.

### H8 · Drop-on-top-half "Supervisor of X" silently appends as a non-leader when the position is already staffed
`src/ui/command/useOrgDragDrop.ts:394` · category: correctness · verified 3/3
- **Evidence:** the drop zone is typed `{ type: 'lead' } // become this position's supervisor`, the ghost says `Supervisor of ${title}`, and `RosterStrip` documents "top half = supervisor". But `commitDrop` only emits `ResourceAssigned` (line 394/406), and the reducer **appends** (`orgReducer.ts:76 assignedResources: [...p.assignedResources, resource]`) while the leader is strictly index 0 (`resource.ts:7`). `splitFor` (line 469) offers the "supervisor" affordance regardless of occupancy, and no event promotes a resource to index 0.
- **Failure:** IC drags Chief Alvarez onto the top half of "Shoring Group" (led by Lt Kim); the ghost reads "Supervisor of Shoring Group". On drop Alvarez is appended at index 1 — the org chart, NodeSheet "· leader" tag, SitStat rail and ICS-201 brief all still show Lt Kim. On the IC root the same drop leaves the old IC as commander of record with no warning and no transfer record. There is no reorder UI, so the only fix is clearing and re-adding in order.

## Refuted (4) — investigated and dropped

- **Grouped un-deploy swallows partial failures** (`StepBackConfirmModal.tsx:60`) — the swallow code is present but unreachable: the caller pre-filters members to `status==='process'`, so a partial success/failure split can't occur.
- **Two-admin mutual demote/revoke race reaches zero admins** (`rules.ts:213`) — cannot: RTDB serializes writes on one timeline and each write's rule reads live committed root state, so the count-free ≥1-admin guard holds in every interleaving.
- **`leafValidate` silently drops non-length ZodString checks** (`rules.ts:43`) — real code behavior, but grep-confirmed **zero** current schemas use regex/email/uuid, so no rule is dropped today. *Latent* footgun if such a check is added later; not a present defect.
- **audit-#2 secured↔returned guard added to `groupAdvance` only, not `shorePointReducer`** (`shorepoint/reducer.ts:305`) — the divergence is **verifiably real** but refuted on reachability: the `ShorePointStatusChanged` branch is off the live path (status changes route through `groupAdvance`). Flagged as a real-but-dormant consistency hazard — a future caller of that branch would resurrect it.

completed, 0 retries needed after the resume). Verified-clean highlights worth recording:

- **core-load:** the #410-1 unfloored-capacity fix is **complete** — `capacity`, `capacityAll`, and the LongShore unrated-zone gate all use the unfloored `exactLength`; the ⅛″ floor is confined to geometric fit/display. Safety-math engine core is sound.

- **post-audit-diff:** the four #410 fix commits verified against the actual code — 103a96e (capacity truth), 54ceb80 (persistent flag), 79172b9 (fan-out + delete guard), 74471ab (mediums/plausibles) — **each landed, but two are incomplete** (H3 fan-out for mixed-status; H7 delete guard bypassed by commitMany; H2 flag not carried into the new views).
- **config-rules:** Firebase-never-cached invariant (ADR-007) holds — the Workbox route matches the app's actual `firebaseio.com` databaseURL for both websocket and long-poll.

**Thin spots (as in June):** concurrency under the *real* Firebase transport — several sync findings
(deploy-after-delete race, applyRemoteRow re-type, first-merge dead-letter) go live the moment the
deferred transport wires listeners; re-audit at that milestone.

## Phase J gate mapping (#138)

| #138 criterion | This review's bearing |
|---|---|
| Feature parity with v3 + approved improvements (#256) | **H2** (flag lost in new views) and the cross-view length collision are v3-parity regressions from the tri-view redesign. |
| Audits clean — XSS/security (#257) | Security-rule cluster: **H4**, invite-code irrevocable, v3 legacy rules deployed, ADMIN self-promote, CSV injection. Fix before this gate can pass. |
| Audits clean — accessibility WCAG (#258) | Four a11y items (lockstep announce, DockDrawer Esc, native-controls no-op, AT-blind plate picker) feed this gate. |
| Audits clean — SME (#260) | Safety-verdict cluster **H1/H2/H3** + Lows (zero-load "ok", plateHeight 0″) are the SME-relevant set. |
| Migration validated on real data (#264) | **H5/H6** (dept create/join no retry) will bite during any real multi-device migration; validate against them. |

**Verdict: not yet.** Close the 8 High + the security-rule Mediums, re-verify the safety cluster
against *real-engine* tests (not the mocked verdict surfaces), and the mechanical foundation is
already cutover-grade.
